summary: Gmail is easy for yourself and your own Workspace org and very hard for the public. Internal apps and Testing-mode apps work in under an hour, but Testing caps you at 100 named test users whose Gmail grants expire every 7 days. A public agent that reads or modifies mail needs Google's restricted-scope verification (Google's own estimate: about 6 weeks, not guaranteed) plus an annual CASA security assessment you arrange and usually pay for; send-only (gmail.send) is sensitive and avoids CASA.

artifacts.title: Scope justification (draft)
artifacts.content:
**https://www.googleapis.com/auth/gmail.readonly** *(use instead of modify if the agent never writes)*
<App> is an AI email assistant. When the user asks it to "summarize unread mail from today" or "find the invoice from Acme", <App> calls `users.messages.list` and `users.messages.get` to fetch the matching messages and shows the summary or result in the <App> chat window. Reading message bodies is the core feature, so `gmail.metadata` (headers and labels only) is not enough: the agent could not summarize content or pull out details.

**https://www.googleapis.com/auth/gmail.modify**
The user can tell <App> to "archive these newsletters", "label this thread Follow-up", or "draft a reply". <App> calls `users.messages.modify` / `users.threads.modify` to add or remove labels and archive, and `users.drafts.create` to save reply drafts the user reviews before sending. `gmail.readonly` cannot change labels or create drafts, and `gmail.labels` cannot read the messages it would apply labels to. <App> never permanently deletes mail, which is why we do not request `https://mail.google.com/`.

**https://www.googleapis.com/auth/gmail.send**
After the user approves a draft in the <App> UI, <App> calls `users.messages.send` to send it from the user's address. This is the narrowest scope that allows sending.

*Data handling (same for all scopes):* Gmail data is processed only to carry out the request the user made, is not sold or used for ads, is not read by <App> staff without the user's explicit permission, and is not used to train or improve generalized AI models. <If applicable: name the LLM API provider and state that it does not train on API data and retains it for at most N days.>

> Edit every sentence so it matches what your product really does. Remove any scope whose feature is not live yet.

artifacts.title: Demo video shot list
artifacts.content:
Target 3-6 minutes, unlisted YouTube, production build, English UI, narration or captions.

1. **Homepage** at https://<yourdomain>/ showing the app name (same as on the consent screen) and the privacy policy link.
2. **Start connect**: click "Connect Gmail" in your app (Google-branded button per Google branding guidelines).
3. **Consent screen**: pause on the full Google consent screen. Zoom into the browser address bar so the `client_id=` value is readable and matches the project you submitted. Language selector (bottom-left) set to English. Every requested scope is visible.
4. **Return to app** after consent (this is the Composio callback, then your app).
5. **Feature per scope**, saying the scope name out loud or in a caption:
   - gmail.readonly: ask the agent to summarize today's unread mail; show the result.
   - gmail.modify: ask it to label/archive a thread; switch to Gmail and show the label applied; show a draft it created.
   - gmail.send: approve a reply in your UI; show it in Gmail's Sent folder.
6. **AI data use** (if any): show where the user is told that their email is processed by an AI model, and any consent toggle.
7. **Revoke / delete**: show how a user disconnects Gmail and requests deletion of their data.

Re-record if the app name, logo, scopes or client ID change before submission.

artifacts.title: Limited Use disclosure and privacy-policy Gmail section
artifacts.content:
**Homepage or privacy policy, verbatim Google-suggested statement (fill in your app name):**

> <App>'s use and transfer of information received from Google APIs will adhere to the [Google API Services User Data Policy](https://developers.google.com/terms/api-services-user-data-policy), including the Limited Use requirements.

**Gmail data section (draft, get legal review):**

- *What we access:* With your permission, <App> accesses your Gmail messages, labels and drafts (scopes: <list>) only to perform the actions you ask the assistant to take.
- *How we use it:* To show summaries and search results, apply labels you request, create drafts, and send messages you approve. We do not use Gmail data for advertising, do not sell it, and do not use it to determine credit-worthiness.
- *AI processing:* Message content is sent to <LLM provider> solely to generate the response you requested. Neither <App> nor <provider> uses your Gmail data to train or improve generalized or foundation AI models.
- *Human access:* <App> staff do not read your email unless you explicitly ask us to (for example in a support request), it is needed for security (investigating abuse), or required by law.
- *Sharing:* We share Gmail data only with the sub-processors needed to provide the feature (<Composio> for OAuth token storage and API calls, <LLM provider>, <hosting>), each bound to these same limits.
- *Storage and deletion:* We keep <what> for <how long>. Disconnect Gmail in Settings or email <privacy@yourdomain> and we delete stored Gmail data within <N> days.

Also show a short in-product notice next to the Connect Gmail button summarizing the above.

openQuestions: Redirect URI domain: Google requires every domain used in client configuration to be an authorized domain and requires you to verify ownership of all authorized domains. Does a redirect URI on Composio's host block verification, and does Composio support a callback on the developer's own domain?

Google's create-credentials page says 'client secrets aren't used for Web applications', while the OAuth 2.0 overview says a web server application requires a secret. Confirm in the console that a Web application client still issues a secret that Composio can use.

What does the 'Use this client for an AI-powered agent' option on OAuth client creation change (consent screen, verification, token behaviour)? It cannot be changed after creation; should Composio-backed agents tick it?

Current CASA pricing and duration: Google charges nothing and leaves price to the assessor; the ADA Tier 2 page says self-scanning is deprecated in favour of lab-verified scans, while Google's FAQ still mentions a 'free tier 2 assessment'. Which assurance level (AL1 vs AL2) a new, small app is assigned is not published.
Is a paid Google Workspace subscription strictly required for the Internal scenario, or does a free Cloud Identity organization work the same for Gmail (Gmail itself requires Workspace)?
Gmail API pricing: no billing was required in Google's described flow, but no fetched page explicitly states the Gmail API is free.
